subtopics.title: Volume of right prisms
subtopics.exposition: Volume is the three dimensional space occupied by an object, or the contents of an object. The volume of a right prism is calculated by multiplying the area of the base of the solid by the height of the solid. For a rectangular prism, the base is a rectangle, so volume = area of base × height = area of rectangle × height = l × b × h. For a triangular prism, the base is a triangle, so volume = area of base × height = area of triangle × height = (1/2 b × h) × H. To find the volume of a cube, first find the area of the base: the base is a square, with area s² (for a side of 3 this is 3² = 9 cm²). Next, multiply the area of the base by the height of the solid to find the volume: for the cube, 9 × 3 = 27 cm³. To find the volume of a triangular prism, first find the area of the base: the base is a triangle, with area 1/2 b × h. Substituting b = 8 and h = 10 into the area of the triangle gives (1/2 × 8) × 10 = 40 cm². Next, multiply the area of the base by the height of the prism: 40 × 20 = 800 cm³. Volume is measured in cubic units. The final answer is written as a statement of the volume in cubic units: the volume of the cube is 27 cm³. The final answer is written as a statement of the volume in cubic units: the volume of the triangular prism is 800 cm³.

subtopics.title: Volume of a cylinder
subtopics.exposition: The volume of a cylinder is calculated by multiplying the area of the base of the solid by the height of the solid. For a cylinder, the base is a circle, so volume = area of base × height = area of circle × height = πr² × h. To find the volume of a cylinder, first find the area of the base: the base is a circle, with area πr². Substituting r = 4 into the area of the circle gives π(4)² = 16π cm², leaving the base area in terms of π. Next, multiply the area of the base by the height of the cylinder: volume = πr² × h = 16π × 15, which is approximately 754.0 cm³. When the question asks for the volume correct to 1 decimal place, the value of 16π × 15 is rounded to 1 decimal place, giving approximately 754.0 cm³ (the book writes the decimal with a comma). The final answer is written as a statement of the volume in cubic units: the volume of the cylinder is 754.0 cm³.
